site.name: O Elefante Fugiu
site.description: Short interactive stories from Portuguese history, tied to the map and to time.
site.home_preview_title: O Elefante Fugiu: stories from Portugal’s past
site.home_preview_description: Short stories from Portuguese history, from ancient times to the 20th century. Each takes a minute to read and comes with sources and a place you can still visit today. Free, no ads.
site.preview_alt_home: The project’s mascot, an elephant in a blue coat with a cane, on a light azulejo pattern.
site.preview_alt_page: A light azulejo pattern with no text.
site.preview_alt_thread: A light pattern of azulejo diamonds with a band in the color of the thread along the bottom.

about.title: About the project
about.description: Short, sourced stories from Portugal’s past, each tied to a real place you can visit. Meet the one-person project behind O Elefante Fugiu.

method.title: Method and sources
method.description: How I separate proven fact from legend: three labels, sources under every story, and how I handle dates, numbers, images, and mistakes.

report.title: Found a mistake?
report.description: Spotted a wrong date, name, or place in a story? Tell me, and I’ll check it.

share.title: Know a story?
share.description: Did something little known happen in your town, or does a strange tradition live on there? Tell me, and I’ll check the sources and maybe make it a story.

legal.title: Legal information
legal.description: How you may reuse the texts, illustrations and code, what your browser stores, and which services see your IP address. No cookies, no ads.

map.title: Map
map.description: Explore Portuguese history on a map: filter stories by era or thread, then find your way to the spot where each one happened.

surprise.title: Surprise me
surprise.description: Not sure where to start? Get a random story from Portugal’s past in seconds.

myths.title: Myth or fact
myths.description: What guides, guidebooks, and friends say about Portugal: pick what you think, then read what really happened. Behind every answer is one of my stories.

order.title: Which came first?
order.description: A game: two events from Portugal’s past, which came first? Ten pairs and a result. Behind every date there is one of my stories.

games.title: Games
games.description: Myth or fact and “Which came first?”: short games about Portuguese history, and after every answer the whole story.

home.hook_title: In 1515 a king set a rhinoceros against an elephant. The elephant ran away.
home.intro: That is where the name comes from: O Elefante Fugiu, “the elephant ran away.” Stories from Portugal’s past, each a one-minute read tied to a place you can visit.
home.threads_intro: Pick a theme and follow it through the centuries.
home.how: For walks and trips around Portugal: read the story, then go see the place.
home.myths_line: {stories} about Portugal that tour guides love to tell. Can you guess which ones are true?

report.lead: Even elephants sometimes lose their way. If a story has a wrong date, name, place or translation, let me know. I’ll check it, fix the text and update the date it was last checked.
report.what_hint: For example: the battle was on August 14, not the 15th
report.source_label: Where can I check this? (if you know)
report.source_hint: A link, a book, a museum label
report.email_label: Your email (if you’d like a reply)
report.note: Your message reaches my inbox through the FormSubmit service. I don’t store anything on the site (more in {{legal|Legal information}}). You can also write to me directly: {{email}}.
report.sent_title: Thank you! The elephant is already running to check.
report.sent_text: If you left your email, I’ll write back once I’ve looked into it.
report.failed: Could not send right now. Try again or write to me directly at
report.too_short: Describe the mistake in a few words.

share.lead: Maybe something happened in your town or village that few people know about. Or a strange tradition still lives on there. Tell me. I’ll check the sources and, if it works out, turn it into a story for the site.
share.where_hint: Town, village, or a specific place
share.what_hint: In your own words. A rough year is fine.
share.source_hint: A book, museum, plaque, local tale. A link if you have one.
share.email_label: Your email (if you’d like a reply)
share.subject: Elefante: know a story
share.note: I’ll rewrite the story myself and check it against sources. Your name won’t appear on the site. Your message reaches me by email via FormSubmit; the site stores nothing.
share.sent_text: I read every message. If you left your email, I’ll write back once I’ve looked into it.
share.report_link: Have a new story rather than a fix? This way.
